key_insight: The paper proposes a way to detect adversarially altered medical images by comparing model responses to clean, attacked, and noise-perturbed inputs, including the attack direction.
clinical_relevance: If reliable, this could help protect radiology AI from hidden manipulations that might cause missed findings or false alarms.
method: Uses subsequent random-noise attacks to probe whether an image is adversarial
Compares prediction changes with a Sigmoid-based variation analysis
Checks differences across clean vs. adversarial versions to flag directional attacks
evidence_signal: The approach was tested on three medical imaging datasets and reported up to 99.8% accuracy in identifying adversarial directional attacks across multiple attack scenarios.
watch_item: Performance is reported from abstracted benchmark testing, so real-world robustness and workflow integration still need validation.
paper_title: Robust Detection of Directional Adversarial Attacks in Deep Neural Networks for Radiological Imaging
